source.author: verg
source.text: Proxuma deinde tenent maesti loca, qui sibi letum insontes peperere manu, lucemque perosi proiecere animas.
source.text_original: Proxuma deinde tenent maesti loca, qui sibi letum / insontes peperere manu, lucemque perosi / proiecere animas.
source.text_english: Next the mournful ones hold the nearest places, who, innocent, brought death upon themselves by their own hand and, hating the light, cast away their lives.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: Lazarus recepit mala sua in uita sua et diues ille purpuratus , crassus et nitidus, fruitus est bonis carnis, dum aduiueret, sed diuersa post mortem tenent loca miseriae deliciis et deliciae miseriis commutantur : in nostro arbitrio est uel Lazarum sequi uel diuitem.
reuse.text_original: Lazarus recepit mala sua in uita sua et diues ille purpuratus , crassus et nitidus, fruitus est bonis carnis, dum aduiueret, sed diuersa post mortem tenent loca — miseriae deliciis et deliciae miseriis commutantur —: in nostro arbitrio est uel Lazarum sequi uel diuitem.
reuse.text_english: Lazarus received his evil things in his lifetime, and that rich man, clothed in purple, fat and sleek, enjoyed the good things of the flesh while he lived; but after death they are held in different places, misery is exchanged for delights and delights for miseries: it is within our power either to follow Lazarus or the rich man.
